strengths: Cover letter opening hook is excellent—specific story about sub-section chunking immediately demonstrates relevant domain expertise
Honest acknowledgment of LangGraph gap while emphasizing transferable patterns (state management, tool orchestration, evaluation loops) shows self-awareness and credibility
Strong biopharma/regulated document experience directly relevant to Tempus's R&D focus—Fortune-200 biopharma client work is compelling evidence
Company research is evident and specific: 8M+ de-identified records, 350+ petabytes, majority of top 20 pharma partnerships
Cover letter voice is authentic and opinionated ('precision matters enormously when the stakes are real')—doesn't read AI-generated
Resume skills section is well-targeted: RAG, vector databases, rerankers, document ingestion, LLM evaluation all map to role requirements
weaknesses: LangGraph is explicitly listed as a key skill in job posting but not present in candidate's production experience—gap is acknowledged but still a potential screening risk
Resume bullets could include more quantified business impact (e.g., retrieval accuracy improvements, time savings, error reduction)—current metrics are mostly scale/volume
Education (BA Economics + bootcamp certificate) may raise questions for 'Senior Scientist II' title which often implies advanced degree or research background
Cover letter is three long paragraphs—could benefit from slightly tighter editing for busy reviewers
revision_suggestions: Consider adding one quantified outcome metric to resume: e.g., 'Improved retrieval relevance by X%' or 'Reduced document processing time by Y%' to strengthen impact claims
If you have any exposure to LangGraph (even side projects, tutorials, prototypes), consider mentioning it to reduce the gap concern
The third cover letter paragraph could be trimmed slightly—some redundancy in restating the pilot-to-300-user scale point
